chunks: The day the Resurrection comes the sinners will be overwhelmed with despair.

key_terms.يُبْلِسُ: He will be overwhelmed with despair/silence

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when the sinners are described as 'yublisa' on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'yublisa' (being struck with silence/despair) signifies the total annihilation of the sinners' ability to speak or justify themselves, reflecting the finality of divine judgment. This state contrasts with the 'mu'minun' (believers) who will be granted eloquence and joy, highlighting the eschatological consequence of persistent disbelief (kufr) and moral corruption. The verse serves as a warning that the Day of Resurrection is not merely a physical event but a spiritual reckoning where deeds manifest as internal states of despair.
